final_message:
**Status: verified** (local-full, full precision; every number below comes from that backend).

## What the model computes
It outputs how many of the 6 input tokens are in the same class as the last token, counting the last token itself. The classes are {do, vu}, {ge, no} and {go, ko}, i.e. token ids {2,7}, {3,6}, {4,5}.

```python
cls = {2: 0, 7: 0, 3: 1, 6: 1, 4: 2, 5: 2}
count = sum(cls[t] == cls[tokens[-1]] for t in tokens[1:])
return 8 + count   # digit tokens '0'..'6' are ids 8..14
```

## Circuit: `mlp0` → head `1.1` → `mlp1`
- **`mlp0`** works per token at every input position. Mean-ablating it leaves 0.0 of the metric (E0010); patching it at a single position restores only 0.25–0.43, and 0 at BOS (E0016, E0017).
- **Head `1.1`** attends from the last position uniformly over BOS plus all same-class tokens, so the BOS weight is 1/(1+count). It is exactly 1/7 when all six tokens are class-mates (E0007) and 1/2 when the last token is alone in its class (E0013). Ablating it leaves 0.0 (E0009).
- **`mlp1`** acts only at the last position and produces the digit. Ablating it leaves 0.012 (E0011); patching it at the last position alone restores the full answer (E0016).
- **Not involved:** heads 0.0, 0.1, 0.2, 1.0 and 1.2. Mean-ablating all five together leaves the metric at 1.0 (E0012).

## Verification (V0001, 200 held-out inputs, seed 7)

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `predict()` agrees with the model | 200/200 (null max 0.315) |
| Circuit ablated | 0.0085 of clean metric, accuracy 0.35 |
| Everything except the circuit ablated | 1.0 of clean metric, accuracy 1.0 |
| Random same-size sets ablated | metric stays at 1.0 |

## Predictions and budget
- **Predictions:** 10 pre-registered, 9 confirmed, 0 refuted, 1 inconclusive. The inconclusive one (E0008) was my mistake: I gave a metric path that does not exist for joint ablations. The observed value was 1.0, and I re-ran it on a fresh seed with the same threshold as E0012.
- **Experiments:** 17 of 25 used, 6 of them exploratory.

## Gaps
- The `mlp0` → `1.1` link is inferred from layer order, necessity and the per-position patching. Path patching with an MLP as sender raised an error, so I did not measure whether `mlp0` feeds the head's query, key or both.
- That `mlp0` writes a "class" feature and that `mlp1` reads 1/(1+count) are interpretations consistent with the attention pattern; neither was decoded directly.
- Heads 1.0 and 1.2 show nonzero direct writes along the answer direction (0.21 and 0.19, exploratory E0014), yet ablating them changes nothing. I did not explain what they write.
